q: Which of the following specialties might focus on studying all of the structures of the ankle and foot?
why: The correct answer is: regional anatomy. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: A scientist wants to study how the body uses foods and fluids during a marathon run. This scientist is most likely a(n) ________.
why: The correct answer is: exercise physiologist. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “science that studies the form and composition of the body’s structures”
why: anatomy: science that studies the form and composition of the body’s structures

q: Which term matches this definition? “study of the larger structures of the body, typically with the unaided eye; also referred to macroscopic anatomy”
why: gross anatomy: study of the larger structures of the body, typically with the unaided eye; also referred to macroscopic anatomy

q: Which term matches this definition? “steady state of body systems that living organisms maintain”
why: homeostasis: steady state of body systems that living organisms maintain

q: Which term matches this definition? “study of very small structures of the body using magnification”
why: microscopic anatomy: study of very small structures of the body using magnification

q: Which term matches this definition? “science that studies the chemistry, biochemistry, and physics of the body’s functions”
why: physiology: science that studies the chemistry, biochemistry, and physics of the body’s functions

q: Which term matches this definition? “study of the structures that contribute to specific body regions”
why: regional anatomy: study of the structures that contribute to specific body regions

card.q: Name at least three reasons to study anatomy and physiology.
card.a: An understanding of anatomy and physiology is essential for any career in the health professions. It can also help you make choices that promote your health, respond appropriately to signs of illness, make sense of health-related news, and help you in your roles as a parent, spouse, partner, friend, colleague, and caregiver.

card.q: For whom would an appreciation of the structural characteristics of the human heart come more easily: an alien who lands on Earth, abducts a human, and dissects his heart, or an anatomy and physiology student performing a dissection of the heart on her very first day of class? Why?
card.a: A student would more readily appreciate the structures revealed in the dissection. Even though the student has not yet studied the workings of the heart and blood vessels in her class, she has experienced her heart beating every moment of her life, has probably felt her pulse, and likely has at least a basic understanding of the role of the heart in pumping blood throughout her body. This understanding of the heart’s function (physiology) would support her study of the heart’s form (anatomy).

q: The smallest independently functioning biological unit of an organism is a(n) ________.
why: The correct answer is: cell. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: A collection of similar tissues that performs a specific function is an ________.
why: The correct answer is: organ. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The body system responsible for structural support and movement is the ________.
why: The correct answer is: skeletal system. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “smallest independently functioning unit of all organisms; in animals, a cell contains cytoplasm, composed of fluid and organelles”
why: cell: smallest independently functioning unit of all organisms; in animals, a cell contains cytoplasm, composed of fluid and organelles

q: Which term matches this definition? “functionally distinct structure composed of two or more types of tissues”
why: organ: functionally distinct structure composed of two or more types of tissues

q: Which term matches this definition? “group of organs that work together to carry out a particular function”
why: organ system: group of organs that work together to carry out a particular function

q: Which term matches this definition? “living being that has a cellular structure and that can independently perform all physiologic functions necessary for life”
why: organism: living being that has a cellular structure and that can independently perform all physiologic functions necessary for life

q: Which term matches this definition? “group of similar or closely related cells that act together to perform a specific function”
why: tissue: group of similar or closely related cells that act together to perform a specific function

card.q: Name the six levels of organization of the human body.
card.a: Chemical, cellular, tissue, organ, organ system, organism.

card.q: The ovaries and the testes are a part of which body system? Can these organs be members of more than one organ system? Why or why not?
card.a: The female ovaries and the male testes are parts of the reproductive system. But they also secrete hormones, as does the endocrine system, therefore ovaries and testes function within both the endocrine and reproductive systems.

q: Metabolism can be defined as the ________.
options: adjustment by an organism to external or internal changes
process whereby all unspecialized cells become specialized to perform distinct functions
process whereby new cells are formed to replace worn-out cells
sum of all chemical reactions in an organism
why: The correct answer is: sum of all chemical reactions in an organism. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is an important molecule because it ________.
options: stores energy for use by body cells
why: The correct answer is: stores energy for use by body cells. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Cancer cells can be characterized as “generic” cells that perform no specialized body function. Thus cancer cells lack ________.
why: The correct answer is: differentiation. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “assembly of more complex molecules from simpler molecules”
why: anabolism: assembly of more complex molecules from simpler molecules

q: Which term matches this definition? “breaking down of more complex molecules into simpler molecules”
why: catabolism: breaking down of more complex molecules into simpler molecules

q: Which term matches this definition? “changes an organism goes through during its life”
why: development: changes an organism goes through during its life

q: Which term matches this definition? “process by which unspecialized cells become specialized in structure and function”
why: differentiation: process by which unspecialized cells become specialized in structure and function

q: Which term matches this definition? “process of increasing in size”
why: growth: process of increasing in size

q: Which term matches this definition? “sum of all of the body’s chemical reactions”
why: metabolism: sum of all of the body’s chemical reactions

card.q: View this video to learn more about metabolic processes. What kind of catabolism occurs in the heart?
card.a: Fatty acid catabolism.

card.q: Explain why the smell of smoke when you are sitting at a campfire does not trigger alarm, but the smell of smoke in your residence hall does.
card.a: When you are sitting at a campfire, your sense of smell adapts to the smell of smoke. Only if that smell were to suddenly and dramatically intensify would you be likely to notice and respond. In contrast, the smell of even a trace of smoke would be new and highly unusual in your residence hall, and would be perceived as danger.

card.q: Identify three different ways that growth can occur in the human body.
card.a: Growth can occur by increasing the number of existing cells, increasing the size of existing cells, or increasing the amount of non-cellular material around cells.

q: Humans have the most urgent need for a continuous supply of ________.
why: The correct answer is: oxygen. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following statements about nutrients is true?
options: All classes of nutrients are essential to human survival.
Because the body cannot store any micronutrients, they need to be consumed nearly every day.
Carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins are micronutrients.
why: The correct answer is: All classes of nutrients are essential to human survival.. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: C.J. is stuck in their car during a bitterly cold blizzard. Their body responds to the cold by ________.
options: increasing the blood to the hands and feet
why: The correct answer is: breaking down stored energy. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “chemical obtained from foods and beverages that is critical to human survival”
why: nutrient: chemical obtained from foods and beverages that is critical to human survival

q: Which term matches this definition? “force exerted by a substance in contact with another substance”
why: pressure: force exerted by a substance in contact with another substance

card.q: When you open a bottle of sparkling water, the carbon dioxide gas in the bottle form bubbles. If the bottle is left open, the water will eventually “go flat.” Explain these phenomena in terms of atmospheric pressure.
card.a: In a sealed bottle of sparkling water, carbon dioxide gas is kept dissolved in the water under a very high pressure. When you open the bottle, the pressure of the gas above the liquid changes from artificially high to normal atmospheric pressure. The dissolved carbon dioxide gas expands, and rises in bubbles to the surface. When a bottle of sparkling water is left open, it eventually goes flat because its gases continue to move out of solution until the pressure in the water is approximately equal to atmospheric pressure.

card.q: On his midsummer trek through the desert, Josh ran out of water. Why is this particularly dangerous?
card.a: The primary way that the body responds to high environmental heat is by sweating; however, sweating requires water, which comes from body fluids, including blood plasma. If Josh becomes dehydrated, he will be unable to sweat adequately to cool his body, and he will be at risk for heat stroke as his blood pressure drops too much from the loss of water from the blood plasma.

q: After you eat lunch, nerve cells in your stomach respond to the distension (the stimulus) resulting from the food. They relay this information to ________.
why: The correct answer is: a control center. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Stimulation of the heat-loss center causes ________.
options: blood vessels in the skin to constrict
breathing to become slow and shallow
sweat glands to increase their output
why: The correct answer is: sweat glands to increase their output. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following is an example of a normal physiologic process that uses a positive feedback loop?
why: The correct answer is: childbirth. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “compares values to their normal range; deviations cause the activation of an effector”
why: control center: compares values to their normal range; deviations cause the activation of an effector

q: Which term matches this definition? “organ that can cause a change in a value”
why: effector: organ that can cause a change in a value

q: Which term matches this definition? “homeostatic mechanism that tends to stabilize an upset in the body’s physiological condition by preventing an excessive response to a stimulus, typically as the stimulus is removed”
why: negative feedback: homeostatic mechanism that tends to stabilize an upset in the body’s physiological condition by preventing an excessive response to a stimulus, typically as the stimulus is removed

q: Which term matches this definition? “range of values around the set point that do not cause a reaction by the control center”
why: normal range: range of values around the set point that do not cause a reaction by the control center

q: Which term matches this definition? “mechanism that intensifies a change in the body’s physiological condition in response to a stimulus”
why: positive feedback: mechanism that intensifies a change in the body’s physiological condition in response to a stimulus

q: Which term matches this definition? “(also, receptor) reports a monitored physiological value to the control center”
why: sensor: (also, receptor) reports a monitored physiological value to the control center

card.q: Water concentration in the body is critical for proper functioning. A person’s body retains very tight control on water levels without conscious control by the person. Watch this video to learn more about water concentration in the body. Which organ has primary control over the amount of water in the body?
card.a: The kidneys.

card.q: Identify the four components of a negative feedback loop and explain what would happen if secretion of a body chemical controlled by a negative feedback system became too great.
card.a: The four components of a negative feedback loop are: stimulus, sensor, control center, and effector. If too great a quantity of the chemical were excreted, sensors would activate a control center, which would in turn activate an effector. In this case, the effector (the secreting cells) would be adjusted downward.

card.q: What regulatory processes would your body use if you were trapped by a blizzard in an unheated, uninsulated cabin in the woods?
card.a: Any prolonged exposure to extreme cold would activate the brain’s heat-gain center. This would reduce blood flow to your skin, and shunt blood returning from your limbs away from the digits and into a network of deep veins. Your brain’s heat-gain center would also increase your muscle contraction, causing you to shiver. This increases the energy consumption of skeletal muscle and generates more heat. Your body would also produce thyroid hormone and epinephrine, chemicals that promote increased metabolism and heat production.

q: What is the position of the body when it is in the “normal anatomical position?”
options: The person is prone with upper limbs, including palms, touching sides and lower limbs touching at sides.
The person is standing facing the observer, with upper limbs extended out at a ninety-degree angle from the torso and lower limbs in a wide stance with feet pointing laterally
The person is supine with upper limbs, including palms, touching sides and lower limbs touching at sides.
why: The correct answer is: None of the above. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: To make a banana split, you halve a banana into two long, thin, right and left sides along the ________.
why: The correct answer is: midsagittal plane. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The lumbar region is ________.
why: The correct answer is: superior to the popliteal region. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The heart is within the ________.
why: The correct answer is: mediastinum. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “division of the anterior (ventral) cavity that houses the abdominal and pelvic viscera”
why: abdominopelvic cavity: division of the anterior (ventral) cavity that houses the abdominal and pelvic viscera

q: Which term matches this definition? “standard reference position used for describing locations and directions on the human body”
why: anatomical position: standard reference position used for describing locations and directions on the human body

q: Which term matches this definition? “describes the front or direction toward the front of the body; also referred to as ventral”
why: anterior: describes the front or direction toward the front of the body; also referred to as ventral

q: Which term matches this definition? “describes a position below or lower than another part of the body proper; near or toward the tail (in humans, the coccyx, or lowest part of the spinal column); also referred to as inferior”
why: caudal: describes a position below or lower than another part of the body proper; near or toward the tail (in humans, the coccyx, or lowest part of the spinal column); also referred to as inferior

q: Which term matches this definition? “describes a position above or higher than another part of the body proper; also referred to as superior”
why: cranial: describes a position above or higher than another part of the body proper; also referred to as superior

q: Which term matches this definition? “division of the posterior (dorsal) cavity that houses the brain”
why: cranial cavity: division of the posterior (dorsal) cavity that houses the brain

card.q: In which direction would an MRI scanner move to produce sequential images of the body in the frontal plane, and in which direction would an MRI scanner move to produce sequential images of the body in the sagittal plane?
card.a: If the body were supine or prone, the MRI scanner would move from top to bottom to produce frontal sections, which would divide the body into anterior and posterior portions, as in “cutting” a deck of cards. Again, if the body were supine or prone, to produce sagittal sections, the scanner would move from left to right or from right to left to divide the body lengthwise into left and right portions.

card.q: If a bullet were to penetrate a lung, which three anterior thoracic body cavities would it enter, and which layer of the serous membrane would it encounter first?
card.a: The bullet would enter the ventral, thoracic, and pleural cavities, and it would encounter the parietal layer of serous membrane first.

q: In 1901, Wilhelm Röntgen was the first person to win the Nobel Prize for physics. For what discovery did he win?
options: the link between radiation and cancer
why: The correct answer is: X-rays. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following imaging techniques would be best to use to study the uptake of nutrients by rapidly multiplying cancer cells?
why: The correct answer is: PET. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following imaging studies can be used most safely during pregnancy?
why: The correct answer is: ultrasounds. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: What are two major disadvantages of MRI scans?
options: release of radiation and poor quality images
high cost and the need for shielding from the magnetic signals
can only view metabolically active tissues and inadequate availability of equipment
release of radiation and the need for a patient to be confined to metal tube for up to 30 minutes
why: The correct answer is: high cost and the need for shielding from the magnetic signals. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “medical imaging technique in which a computer-enhanced cross-sectional X-ray image is obtained”
why: computed tomography (CT): medical imaging technique in which a computer-enhanced cross-sectional X-ray image is obtained

q: Which term matches this definition? “medical imaging technique in which a device generates a magnetic field to obtain detailed sectional images of the internal structures of the body”
why: magnetic resonance imaging (MRI): medical imaging technique in which a device generates a magnetic field to obtain detailed sectional images of the internal structures of the body

q: Which term matches this definition? “medical imaging technique in which radiopharmaceuticals are traced to reveal metabolic and physiological functions in tissues”
why: positron emission tomography (PET): medical imaging technique in which radiopharmaceuticals are traced to reveal metabolic and physiological functions in tissues

q: Which term matches this definition? “application of ultrasonic waves to visualize subcutaneous body structures such as tendons and organs”
why: ultrasonography: application of ultrasonic waves to visualize subcutaneous body structures such as tendons and organs

q: Which term matches this definition? “form of high energy electromagnetic radiation with a short wavelength capable of penetrating solids and ionizing gases; used in medicine as a diagnostic aid to visualize body structures such as bones”
why: X-ray: form of high energy electromagnetic radiation with a short wavelength capable of penetrating solids and ionizing gases; used in medicine as a diagnostic aid to visualize body structures such as bones

card.q: A patient undergoing an MRI is surrounded by a tube-shaped scanner. Watch this video to learn more about MRIs. What is the function of magnets in an MRI?
card.a: The magnets induce tissue to emit radio signals that can show differences between different types of tissue.

card.q: PET relies on radioactive substances administered several minutes before the scan. Watch this video to learn more about PET. How is PET used in chemotherapy?
card.a: PET scans can indicate how patients are responding to chemotherapy.

card.q: Which medical imaging technique is most dangerous to use repeatedly, and why?
card.a: CT scanning subjects patients to much higher levels of radiation than X-rays, and should not be performed repeatedly.

card.q: Explain why ultrasound imaging is the technique of choice for studying fetal growth and development.
card.a: Ultrasonography does not expose a mother or fetus to radiation, to radiopharmaceuticals, or to magnetic fields. At this time, there are no known medical risks of ultrasonography.

q: Together, just four elements make up more than 95 percent of the body’s mass. These include ________.
why: The correct answer is: oxygen, carbon, hydrogen, and nitrogen. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The smallest unit of an element that still retains the distinctive behavior of that element is an ________.
why: The correct answer is: atom. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The characteristic that gives an element its distinctive properties is its number of ________.
why: The correct answer is: protons. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: On the periodic table of the elements, mercury (Hg) has an atomic number of 80 and a mass number of 200.59. It has seven stable isotopes. The most abundant of these probably have ________.
why: The correct answer is: more than 80 neutrons each. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Nitrogen has an atomic number of seven. How many electron shells does it likely have?
why: The correct answer is: two. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

card.q: Visit this website to view the periodic table. In the periodic table of the elements, elements in a single column have the same number of electrons that can participate in a chemical reaction. These electrons are known as “valence electrons.” For example, the elements in the first column all have a single valence electron—an electron that can be “donated” in a chemical reaction with another atom. What is the meaning of a mass number shown in parentheses?
card.a: The mass number is the total number of protons and neutrons in the nucleus of an atom.

card.q: The most abundant elements in the foods and beverages you consume are oxygen, carbon, hydrogen, and nitrogen. Why might having these elements in consumables be useful?
card.a: These four elements—oxygen, carbon, hydrogen, and nitrogen—together make up more than 95 percent of the mass of the human body, and the body cannot make elements, so it is helpful to have them in consumables.

card.q: Oxygen, whose atomic number is eight, has three stable isotopes: ¹⁶O, ¹⁷O, and ¹⁸O. Explain what this means in terms of the number of protons and neutrons.
card.a: Oxygen has eight protons. In its most abundant stable form, it has eight neutrons, too, for a mass number of 16. In contrast, ¹⁷O has nine neutrons, and ¹⁸O has 10 neutrons.

card.q: Magnesium is an important element in the human body, especially in bones. Magnesium’s atomic number is 12. Is it stable or reactive? Why? If it were to react with another atom, would it be more likely to accept or to donate one or more electrons?
card.a: Magnesium’s 12 electrons are distributed as follows: two in the first shell, eight in the second shell, and two in its valence shell. According to the octet rule, magnesium is unstable (reactive) because its valence shell has just two electrons. It is therefore likely to participate in chemical reactions in which it donates two electrons.

q: Which of the following is a molecule, but not a compound?
why: The correct answer is: H₂. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: A molecule of ammonia contains one atom of nitrogen and three atoms of hydrogen. These are linked with ________.
why: The correct answer is: polar covalent bonds. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: When an atom donates an electron to another atom, it becomes
why: The correct answer is: an ion. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: A substance formed of crystals of equal numbers of cations and anions held together by ionic bonds is called a(n) ________.
why: The correct answer is: salt. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following statements about chemical bonds is true?
options: Covalent bonds are stronger than ionic bonds in biological systems.
Hydrogen bonds occur between two atoms of hydrogen.
Bonding readily occurs between nonpolar and polar molecules.
A molecule of water is unlikely to bond with an ion.
why: The correct answer is: Covalent bonds are stronger than ionic bonds in biological systems.. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

card.q: Visit this website to learn about electrical energy and the attraction/repulsion of charges. What happens to a can lying on its side when a balloon that was rubbed against one’s hair is placed close to the can? What happens to the can when the side opposite the balloon is touched with one’s finger while placing the balloon close to it?
card.a: The plastic sheets jump to the nail (the conductor), because the conductor takes on electrons from the electroscope, reducing the repellant force of the two sheets.

card.q: Explain why CH₄ is one of the most common molecules found in nature. Are the bonds between the atoms ionic or covalent?
card.a: A carbon atom has four electrons in its valence shell. According to the octet rule, it will readily participate in chemical reactions that result in its valence shell having eight electrons. Hydrogen, with one electron, will complete its valence shell with two. Electron sharing between an atom of carbon and four atoms of hydrogen meets the requirements of all atoms. The bonds are covalent because the electrons are shared: although hydrogen often participates in ionic bonds, carbon does not because it is highly unlikely to donate or accept four electrons.

card.q: In a hurry one day, you merely rinse your lunch dishes with water. As you are drying your salad bowl, you notice that it still has an oily film. Why was the water alone not effective in cleaning the bowl?
card.a: Water is a polar molecule. It has a region of weakly positive charge and a region of weakly negative charge. These regions are attracted to ions as well as to other polar molecules. Oils are nonpolar, and are repelled by water.

card.q: Could two atoms of oxygen engage in ionic bonding? Why or why not?
card.a: Identical atoms have identical electronegativity and cannot form ionic bonds. Oxygen, for example, has six electrons in its valence shell. Neither donating nor accepting the valence shell electrons of the other will result in the oxygen atoms completing their valence shells. Two atoms of the same element always form covalent bonds.

q: The energy stored in a foot of snow on a steep roof is ________.
why: The correct answer is: potential energy. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The bonding of calcium, phosphorus, and other elements produces mineral crystals that are found in bone. This is an example of a(n) ________ reaction.
why: The correct answer is: synthesis. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: AB → A + B is a general notation for a(n) ________ reaction.
why: The correct answer is: decomposition. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: ________ reactions release energy.
why: The correct answer is: Catabolic, exergonic, and decomposition. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following combinations of atoms is most likely to result in a chemical reaction?
why: The correct answer is: hydrogen and hydrogen. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Chewing a bite of bread mixes it with saliva and facilitates its chemical breakdown. This is most likely due to the fact that ________.
options: the inside of the mouth maintains a very high temperature
why: The correct answer is: saliva contains enzymes. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

card.q: AB + CD → AD + BE Is this a legitimate example of an exchange reaction? Why or why not?
card.a: It is not. An exchange reaction might be AB + CD → AC + BD or AB + CD → AD + BC. In all chemical reactions, including exchange reactions, the components of the reactants are identical to the components of the products. A component present among the reactants cannot disappear, nor can a component not present in the reactants suddenly appear in the products.

card.q: When you do a load of laundry, why do you not just drop a bar of soap into the washing machine? In other words, why is laundry detergent sold as a liquid or powder?
card.a: Recall that the greater the surface area of the reactants, the more quickly and easily they will interact. It takes energy to separate particles of a substance. Powder and liquid laundry detergents, with relatively more surface area per unit, can quickly dissolve into their reactive components when added to the water.

q: CH₄ is methane. This compound is ________.
why: The correct answer is: organic. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following is most likely to be found evenly distributed in water in a homogeneous solution?
why: The correct answer is: sodium ions and chloride ions. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Jenny mixes up a batch of pancake batter, then stirs in some chocolate chips. As she is waiting for the first few pancakes to cook, she notices the chocolate chips sinking to the bottom of the clear glass mixing bowl. The chocolate-chip batter is an example of a ________.
why: The correct answer is: suspension. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: A substance dissociates into K⁺ and Cl^– in solution. The substance is a(n) ________.
why: The correct answer is: salt. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Ty is three years old and as a result of a “stomach bug” has been vomiting for about 24 hours. His blood pH is 7.48. What does this mean?
options: Ty’s blood is within the normal range
why: The correct answer is: Ty’s blood is slightly alkaline.. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

card.q: The pH of lemon juice is 2, and the pH of orange juice is 4. Which of these is more acidic, and by how much? What does this mean?
card.a: Lemon juice is one hundred times more acidic than orange juice. This means that lemon juice has a one hundred-fold greater concentration of hydrogen ions.

card.q: During a party, Eli loses a bet and is forced to drink a bottle of lemon juice. Not long thereafter, he begins complaining of having difficulty breathing, and his friends take him to the local emergency room. There, he is given an intravenous solution of bicarbonate. Why?
card.a: Lemon juice, like any acid, releases hydrogen ions in solution. As excessive H⁺ enters the digestive tract and is absorbed into blood, Eli’s blood pH falls below 7.35. Recall that bicarbonate is a buffer, a weak base that accepts hydrogen ions. By administering bicarbonate intravenously, the emergency department physician helps raise Eli’s blood pH back toward neutral.

q: C₆H₁₂O₆is the chemical formula for a ________.
why: The correct answer is: hexose monosaccharide. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: What organic compound do brain cells primarily rely on for fuel?
why: The correct answer is: glucose. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following is a functional group that is part of a building block of proteins?
why: The correct answer is: amino. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: A pentose sugar is a part of the monomer used to build which type of macromolecule?
why: The correct answer is: nucleic acids. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: A phospholipid ________.
options: has both polar and nonpolar regions
is made up of a triglyceride bonded to a phosphate group
is a building block of ATP
can donate both cations and anions in solution
why: The correct answer is: has both polar and nonpolar regions. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: In DNA, nucleotide bonding forms a compound with a characteristic shape known as a(n) ________.
why: The correct answer is: double helix. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Uracil ________.
why: The correct answer is: all of the above. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The ability of an enzyme’s active sites to bind only substrates of compatible shape and charge is known as ________.
why: The correct answer is: specificity. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

card.q: Watch this video to observe the formation of a disaccharide. What happens when water encounters a glycosidic bond?
card.a: The water hydrolyses, or breaks, the glycosidic bond, forming two monosaccharides.

card.q: If the disaccharide maltose is formed from two glucose monosaccharides, which are hexose sugars, how many atoms of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen does maltose contain and why?
card.a: Maltose contains 12 atoms of carbon, but only 22 atoms of hydrogen and 11 atoms of oxygen, because a molecule of water is removed during its formation via dehydration synthesis.

card.q: Once dietary fats are digested and absorbed, why can they not be released directly into the bloodstream?
card.a: All lipids are hydrophobic and unable to dissolve in the watery environment of blood. They are packaged into lipoproteins, whose outer protein envelope enables them to transport fats in the bloodstream.

q: Because they are embedded within the membrane, ion channels are examples of ________.
why: The correct answer is: integral proteins. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The diffusion of substances within a solution tends to move those substances ________ their ________ gradient.
why: The correct answer is: down; concentration. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Ion pumps and phagocytosis are both examples of ________.
why: The correct answer is: active transport. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Choose the answer that best completes the following analogy: Diffusion is to ________ as endocytosis is to ________.
why: The correct answer is: osmosis; pinocytosis. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “form of transport across the cell membrane that requires input of cellular energy”
why: active transport: form of transport across the cell membrane that requires input of cellular energy

q: Which term matches this definition? “describes a molecule that exhibits a difference in polarity between its two ends, resulting in a difference in water solubility”
why: amphipathic: describes a molecule that exhibits a difference in polarity between its two ends, resulting in a difference in water solubility

q: Which term matches this definition? “membrane surrounding all animal cells, composed of a lipid bilayer interspersed with various molecules; also known as plasma membrane”
why: cell membrane: membrane surrounding all animal cells, composed of a lipid bilayer interspersed with various molecules; also known as plasma membrane

q: Which term matches this definition? “membrane-spanning protein that has an inner pore which allows the passage of one or more substances”
why: channel protein: membrane-spanning protein that has an inner pore which allows the passage of one or more substances

q: Which term matches this definition? “difference in the concentration of a substance between two regions”
why: concentration gradient: difference in the concentration of a substance between two regions

q: Which term matches this definition? “movement of a substance from an area of higher concentration to one of lower concentration”
why: diffusion: movement of a substance from an area of higher concentration to one of lower concentration

card.q: Visit this link to see diffusion and how it is propelled by the kinetic energy of molecules in solution. How does temperature affect diffusion rate, and why?
card.a: Higher temperatures speed up diffusion because molecules have more kinetic energy at higher temperatures.

card.q: What materials can easily diffuse through the lipid bilayer, and why?
card.a: Only materials that are relatively small and nonpolar can easily diffuse through the lipid bilayer. Large particles cannot fit in between the individual phospholipids that are packed together, and polar molecules are repelled by the hydrophobic/nonpolar lipids that line the inside of the bilayer.

card.q: Why is receptor-mediated endocytosis said to be more selective than phagocytosis or pinocytosis?
card.a: Receptor-mediated endocytosis is more selective because the substances that are brought into the cell are the specific ligands that could bind to the receptors being endocytosed. Phagocytosis or pinocytosis, on the other hand, have no such receptor-ligand specificity, and bring in whatever materials happen to be close to the membrane when it is enveloped.

card.q: What do osmosis, diffusion, filtration, and the movement of ions away from like charge all have in common? In what way do they differ?
card.a: These four phenomena are similar in the sense that they describe the movement of substances down a particular type of gradient. Osmosis and diffusion involve the movement of water and other substances down their concentration gradients, respectively. Filtration describes the movement of particles down a pressure gradient, and the movement of ions away from like charge describes their movement down their electrical gradient.

q: Choose the term that best completes the following analogy: Cytoplasm is to cytosol as a swimming pool containing chlorine and flotation toys is to ________.
why: The correct answer is: the water. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The rough ER has its name due to what associated structures?
why: The correct answer is: ribosomes. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following is a function of the rough ER?
why: The correct answer is: production of proteins. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following is a feature common to all three components of the cytoskeleton?
options: They all serve to scaffold the organelles within the cell.
They are all characterized by roughly the same diameter.
They are all polymers of protein subunits.
They all help the cell resist compression and tension.
why: The correct answer is: They are all polymers of protein subunits.. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following organelles produces large quantities of ATP when both glucose and oxygen are available to the cell?
why: The correct answer is: mitochondria. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

card.q: Watch this video to learn about the endomembrane system, which includes the rough and smooth ER and the Golgi body as well as lysosomes and vesicles. What is the primary role of the endomembrane system?
card.a: Processing, packaging, and moving materials manufactured by the cell.

card.q: Explain why the structure of the ER, mitochondria, and Golgi apparatus assist their respective functions.
card.a: The structure of the Golgi apparatus is suited to its function because it is a series of flattened membranous discs; substances are modified and packaged in sequential steps as they travel from one disc to the next. The structure of Golgi apparatus also involves a receiving face and a sending face, which organize cellular products as they enter and leave the Golgi apparatus. The ER and the mitochondria both have structural specializations that increase their surface area. In the mitochondria, the inner membrane is extensively folded, which increases surface area for ATP production. Likewise, the ER is elaborately wound throughout the cell, increasing its surface area for functions like lipid synthesis, Ca⁺⁺ storage, and protein synthesis.

card.q: Compare and contrast lysosomes with peroxisomes: name at least two similarities and one difference.
card.a: Peroxisomes and lysosomes are both cellular organelles bound by lipid bilayer membranes, and they both contain many enzymes. However, peroxisomes contain enzymes that detoxify substances by transferring hydrogen atoms and producing H₂O₂, whereas the enzymes in lysosomes function to break down and digest various unwanted materials.

q: The nucleus and mitochondria share which of the following features?
why: The correct answer is: a double cell membrane. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following structures could be found within the nucleolus?
why: The correct answer is: ribosomes. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following sequences on a DNA molecule would be complementary to GCTTATAT?
why: The correct answer is: CGAATATA. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Place the following structures in order from least to most complex organization: chromatin, nucleosome, DNA, chromosome
why: The correct answer is: DNA, nucleosome, chromatin, chromosome. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following is part of the elongation step of DNA synthesis?
options: pulling apart the two DNA strands
attaching complementary nucleotides to the template strand
why: The correct answer is: attaching complementary nucleotides to the template strand. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

card.q: Watch this video to learn about DNA replication. DNA replication proceeds simultaneously at several sites on the same molecule. What separates the base pair at the start of DNA replication?
card.a: an enzyme

card.q: Explain in your own words why DNA replication is said to be “semiconservative”?
card.a: DNA replication is said to be semiconservative because, after replication is complete, one of the two parent DNA strands makes up half of each new DNA molecule. The other half is a newly synthesized strand. Therefore, half (“semi”) of each daughter DNA molecule is from the parent molecule and half is a new molecule.

card.q: Why is it important that DNA replication take place before cell division? What would happen if cell division of a body cell took place without DNA replication, or when DNA replication was incomplete?
card.a: During cell division, one cell divides to produce two new cells. In order for all of the cells in your body to maintain a full genome, each cell must replicate its DNA before it divides so that a full genome can be allotted to each of its offspring cells. If DNA replication did not take place fully, or at all, the offspring cells would be missing some or all of the genome. This could be disastrous if a cell was missing genes necessary for its function and health.

q: Which of the following is not a difference between DNA and RNA?
options: DNA contains thymine whereas RNA contains uracil
DNA contains deoxyribose and RNA contains ribose
DNA contains alternating sugar-phosphate molecules whereas RNA does not contain sugars
RNA is single stranded and DNA is double stranded
why: The correct answer is: DNA contains alternating sugar-phosphate molecules whereas RNA does not contain sugars. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Transcription and translation take place in the ________ and ________, respectively.
why: The correct answer is: nucleus; cytoplasm. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: How many “letters” of an RNA molecule, in sequence, does it take to provide the code for a single amino acid?
why: The correct answer is: 3. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following is not entirely or mostly made out of RNA?
options: the carriers that shuttle amino acids to a growing polypeptide strand
the messenger molecule that provides the code for protein synthesis
why: The correct answer is: the ribosome. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “consecutive sequence of three nucleotides on a tRNA molecule that is complementary to a specific codon on an mRNA molecule”
why: anticodon: consecutive sequence of three nucleotides on a tRNA molecule that is complementary to a specific codon on an mRNA molecule

q: Which term matches this definition? “consecutive sequence of three nucleotides on an mRNA molecule that corresponds to a specific amino acid”
why: codon: consecutive sequence of three nucleotides on an mRNA molecule that corresponds to a specific amino acid

q: Which term matches this definition? “one of the coding regions of an mRNA molecule that remain after splicing”
why: exon: one of the coding regions of an mRNA molecule that remain after splicing

q: Which term matches this definition? “functional length of DNA that provides the genetic information necessary to build a protein”
why: gene: functional length of DNA that provides the genetic information necessary to build a protein

q: Which term matches this definition? “active interpretation of the information coded in a gene to produce a functional gene product”
why: gene expression: active interpretation of the information coded in a gene to produce a functional gene product

q: Which term matches this definition? “non-coding regions of a pre-mRNA transcript that may be removed during splicing”
why: intron: non-coding regions of a pre-mRNA transcript that may be removed during splicing

card.q: Watch this video to learn about ribosomes. The ribosome binds to the mRNA molecule to start translation of its code into a protein. What happens to the small and large ribosomal subunits at the end of translation?
card.a: They separate and move and are free to join translation of other segments of mRNA.

card.q: Briefly explain the similarities between transcription and DNA replication.
card.a: Transcription and DNA replication both involve the synthesis of nucleic acids. These processes share many common features—particularly, the similar processes of initiation, elongation, and termination. In both cases the DNA molecule must be untwisted and separated, and the coding (i.e., sense) strand will be used as a template. Also, polymerases serve to add nucleotides to the growing DNA or mRNA strand. Both processes are signaled to terminate when completed.

card.q: Contrast transcription and translation. Name at least three differences between the two processes.
card.a: Transcription is really a “copy” process and translation is really an “interpretation” process, because transcription involves copying the DNA message into a very similar RNA message whereas translation involves converting the RNA message into the very different amino acid message. The two processes also differ in their location: transcription occurs in the nucleus and translation in the cytoplasm. The mechanisms by which the two processes are performed are also completely different: transcription utilizes polymerase enzymes to build mRNA whereas translation utilizes different kinds of RNA to build protein.

q: Which of the following phases is characterized by preparation for DNA synthesis?
why: The correct answer is: G₁. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: A mutation in the gene for a cyclin protein might result in which of the following?
options: a cell with additional genetic material than normal
a cell with less genetic material than normal
why: The correct answer is: any of the above. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: What is a primary function of tumor suppressor genes?
options: allow the cell to skip certain phases of the cell cycle
why: The correct answer is: stop certain cells from dividing. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “third stage of mitosis (and meiosis), during which sister chromatids separate into two new nuclear regions of a dividing cell”
why: anaphase: third stage of mitosis (and meiosis), during which sister chromatids separate into two new nuclear regions of a dividing cell

q: Which term matches this definition? “life cycle of a single cell, from its birth until its division into two new daughter cells”
why: cell cycle: life cycle of a single cell, from its birth until its division into two new daughter cells

q: Which term matches this definition? “region of attachment for two sister chromatids”
why: centromere: region of attachment for two sister chromatids

q: Which term matches this definition? “cellular structure that organizes microtubules during cell division”
why: centrosome: cellular structure that organizes microtubules during cell division

q: Which term matches this definition? “progress point in the cell cycle during which certain conditions must be met in order for the cell to proceed to a subsequence phase”
why: checkpoint: progress point in the cell cycle during which certain conditions must be met in order for the cell to proceed to a subsequence phase

q: Which term matches this definition? “contractile ring that forms around a cell during cytokinesis that pinches the cell into two halves”
why: cleavage furrow: contractile ring that forms around a cell during cytokinesis that pinches the cell into two halves

card.q: Visit this link to learn about mitosis. Mitosis results in two identical diploid cells. What structures form during prophase?
card.a: the spindle

card.q: What would happen if anaphase proceeded even though the sister chromatids were not properly attached to their respective microtubules and lined up at the metaphase plate?
card.a: One or both of the new daughter cells would accidently receive duplicate chromosomes and/or would be missing certain chromosomes.

card.q: What are cyclins and cyclin-dependent kinases, and how do they interact?
card.a: A cyclin is one of the primary classes of cell cycle control molecules, while a cyclin-dependent kinase (is one of a group of molecules that work together with cyclins to determine progression past cell checkpoints. By interacting with many additional molecules, these triggers push the cell cycle forward unless prevented from doing so by “stop” signals, if for some reason the cell is not ready.

q: Arrange the following terms in order of increasing specialization: oligopotency, pleuripotency, unipotency, multipotency.
why: The correct answer is: pleuripotency, multipotency, oligopotency, unipotency. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which type of stem cell gives rise to red and white blood cells?
why: The correct answer is: hematopoietic. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: What multipotent stem cells from children sometimes banked by parents?

hematopoietic stem cells from red and white blood cells
why: The correct answer is: cells from the umbilical cord and from baby teeth. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “describes the condition of being able to differentiate into different types of cells within a given cell lineage or small number of lineages, such as a red blood cell or white blood cell”
why: multipotent: describes the condition of being able to differentiate into different types of cells within a given cell lineage or small number of lineages, such as a red blood cell or white blood cell

q: Which term matches this definition? “describes the condition of being more specialized than multipotency; the condition of being able to differentiate into one of a few possible cell types”
why: oligopotent: describes the condition of being more specialized than multipotency; the condition of being able to differentiate into one of a few possible cell types

q: Which term matches this definition? “describes the condition of being able to differentiate into a large variety of cell types”
why: pluripotent: describes the condition of being able to differentiate into a large variety of cell types

q: Which term matches this definition? “cell that is oligo-, multi-, or pleuripotent that has the ability to produce additional stem cells rather than becoming further specialized”
why: stem cell: cell that is oligo-, multi-, or pleuripotent that has the ability to produce additional stem cells rather than becoming further specialized

q: Which term matches this definition? “embryonic cells that have the ability to differentiate into any type of cell and organ in the body”
why: totipotent: embryonic cells that have the ability to differentiate into any type of cell and organ in the body

q: Which term matches this definition? “one of the proteins that regulate the transcription of genes”
why: transcription factor: one of the proteins that regulate the transcription of genes

card.q: Explain how a transcription factor ultimately determines whether or not a protein will be present in a given cell?
card.a: Transcription factors bind to DNA and either promote or inhibit the transcription of a gene. If they promote the transcription of a particular gene, then that gene will be transcribed and the mRNA subsequently translated into protein. If gene transcription is inhibited, then there will be no way of synthesizing the gene’s corresponding protein.

card.q: Discuss two reasons why the therapeutic use of embryonic stem cells can present a problem.
card.a: Embryonic stem cells derive from human embryos, which are destroyed to obtain the cells. The destruction of human embryos is an ethical problem. And, the DNA in an embryonic stem cell would differ from the DNA of the person being treated, which could result in immune problems or rejected of tissue.

q: The process by which a less specialized cell matures into a more specialized cell is called ________.
why: The correct answer is: differentiation. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Differentiated cells in a developing embryo derive from ________.
options: connective tissue, epithelial tissue, and muscle tissue

q: Which of the following lines the body cavities exposed to the external environment?
why: The correct answer is: mucosa. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “type of tissue that serves to hold in place, connect, and integrate the body’s organs and systems”
why: connective tissue: type of tissue that serves to hold in place, connect, and integrate the body’s organs and systems

q: Which term matches this definition? “connective tissue that encapsulates organs and lines movable joints”
why: connective tissue membrane: connective tissue that encapsulates organs and lines movable joints

q: Which term matches this definition? “skin; epithelial tissue made up of a stratified squamous epithelial cells that cover the outside of the body”

why: ectoderm: outermost embryonic germ layer from which the epidermis and the nervous tissue derive

q: Which term matches this definition? “innermost embryonic germ layer from which most of the digestive system and lower respiratory system derive”
why: endoderm: innermost embryonic germ layer from which most of the digestive system and lower respiratory system derive

q: Which term matches this definition? “epithelium attached to a layer of connective tissue”
why: epithelial membrane: epithelium attached to a layer of connective tissue

card.q: Explore this genetics website to learn more about stem cells. How do somatic stem cells differ from embryonic stem cells?
card.a: Most somatic stem cells give rise to only a few cell types.

card.q: Identify the four types of tissue in the body, and describe the major functions of each tissue.
card.a: The four types of tissue in the body are epithelial, connective, muscle, and nervous. Epithelial tissue is made of layers of cells that cover the surfaces of the body that come into contact with the exterior world, line internal cavities, and form glands. Connective tissue binds the cells and organs of the body together and performs many functions, especially in the protection, support, and integration of the body. Muscle tissue, which responds to stimulation and contracts to provide movement, is divided into three major types: skeletal (voluntary) muscles, smooth muscles, and the cardiac muscle in the heart. Nervous tissue allows the body to receive signals and transmit information as electric impulses from one region of the body to another.

card.q: The zygote is described as totipotent because it ultimately gives rise to all the cells in your body including the highly specialized cells of your nervous system. Describe this transition, discussing the steps and processes that lead to these specialized cells.
card.a: The zygote divides into many cells. As these cells become specialized, they lose their ability to differentiate into all tissues. At first they form the three primary germ layers. Following the cells of the ectodermal germ layer, they too become more restricted in what they can form. Ultimately, some of these ectodermal cells become further restricted and differentiate in to nerve cells.

card.q: What is the function of synovial membranes?
card.a: Synovial membranes are a type of connective tissue membrane that supports mobility in joints. The membrane lines the joint cavity and contains fibroblasts that produce hyaluronan, which leads to the production of synovial fluid, a natural lubricant that enables the bones of a joint to move freely against one another.

q: In observing epithelial cells under a microscope, the cells are arranged in a single layer and look tall and narrow, and the nucleus is located close to the basal side of the cell. The specimen is what type of epithelial tissue?
why: The correct answer is: columnar. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following is the epithelial tissue that lines the interior of blood vessels?
why: The correct answer is: simple squamous. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which type of epithelial tissue specializes in moving particles across its surface?
why: The correct answer is: pseudostratified ciliated columnar. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The ________ exocrine gland stores its secretion until the glandular cell ruptures, whereas the ________ gland releases its apical region and reforms.
why: The correct answer is: holocrine; apocrine. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “mechanically attaches adjacent cells to each other or to the basement membrane”
why: anchoring junction: mechanically attaches adjacent cells to each other or to the basement membrane

q: Which term matches this definition? “that part of a cell or tissue which, in general, faces an open space”
why: apical: that part of a cell or tissue which, in general, faces an open space

q: Which term matches this definition? “release of a substance along with the apical portion of the cell”
why: apocrine secretion: release of a substance along with the apical portion of the cell

q: Which term matches this definition? “thin extracellular layer that lies underneath epithelial cells and separates them from other tissues”
why: basal lamina: thin extracellular layer that lies underneath epithelial cells and separates them from other tissues

q: Which term matches this definition? “in epithelial tissue, a thin layer of fibrous material that anchors the epithelial tissue to the underlying connective tissue; made up of the basal lamina and reticular lamina”
why: basement membrane: in epithelial tissue, a thin layer of fibrous material that anchors the epithelial tissue to the underlying connective tissue; made up of the basal lamina and reticular lamina

q: Which term matches this definition? “point of cell-to-cell contact that connects one cell to another in a tissue”
why: cell junction: point of cell-to-cell contact that connects one cell to another in a tissue

card.q: Watch this video to find out more about the anatomy of epithelial tissues. Where in the body would one find non-keratinizing stratified squamous epithelium?
card.a: The inside of the mouth, esophagus, vaginal canal, and anus.

card.q: The structure of a tissue usually is optimized for its function. Describe how the structure of the mucosa and its cells match its function of nutrient absorption.
card.a: The mucosa of the intestine is highly folded, increasing the surface area for nutrient absorption. A greater surface area for absorption allows more nutrients to be absorbed per unit time. In addition, the nutrient-absorbing cells of the mucosa have finger-like projections called microvilli that further increase the surface area for nutrient absorption.

q: Connective tissue is made of which three essential components?
options: cells, ground substance, and carbohydrate fibers
cells, ground substance, and protein fibers
collagen, ground substance, and protein fibers
why: The correct answer is: cells, ground substance, and protein fibers. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Under the microscope, a tissue specimen shows cells located in spaces scattered in a transparent background. This is probably ________.
why: The correct answer is: hyaline cartilage. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which connective tissue specializes in storage of fat?
why: The correct answer is: adipose tissue. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Ligaments connect bones together and withstand a lot of stress. What type of connective tissue should you expect ligaments to contain?
why: The correct answer is: dense regular connective tissue. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: In adults, new connective tissue cells originate from the ________.
why: The correct answer is: mesenchyme. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: In bone, the main cells are ________.
why: The correct answer is: osteocytes. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

card.q: One of the main functions of connective tissue is to integrate organs and organ systems in the body. Discuss how blood fulfills this role.
card.a: Blood is a fluid connective tissue, a variety of specialized cells that circulate in a watery fluid containing salts, nutrients, and dissolved proteins in a liquid extracellular matrix. Blood contains formed elements derived from bone marrow. Erythrocytes, or red blood cells, transport the gases oxygen and carbon dioxide. Leukocytes, or white blood cells, are responsible for the defense of the organism against potentially harmful microorganisms or molecules. Platelets are cell fragments involved in blood clotting. Some cells have the ability to cross the endothelial layer that lines vessels and enter adjacent tissues. Nutrients, salts, and waste are dissolved in the liquid matrix and transported through the body.

card.q: Why does an injury to cartilage, especially hyaline cartilage, heal much more slowly than a bone fracture?
card.a: A layer of dense irregular connective tissue covers cartilage. No blood vessels supply cartilage tissue. Injuries to cartilage heal very slowly because cells and nutrients needed for repair diffuse slowly to the injury site.

q: Striations, cylindrical cells, and multiple nuclei are observed in ________.
why: The correct answer is: skeletal muscle only. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The cells of muscles, myocytes, develop from ________.
why: The correct answer is: myoblasts. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Skeletal muscle is composed of very hard working cells. Which organelles do you expect to find in abundance in skeletal muscle cell?
why: The correct answer is: mitochondria. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “heart muscle, under involuntary control, composed of striated cells that attach to form fibers, each cell contains a single nucleus, contracts autonomously”
why: cardiac muscle: heart muscle, under involuntary control, composed of striated cells that attach to form fibers, each cell contains a single nucleus, contracts autonomously

q: Which term matches this definition? “usually attached to bone, under voluntary control, each cell is a fiber that is multinucleated and striated”
why: skeletal muscle: usually attached to bone, under voluntary control, each cell is a fiber that is multinucleated and striated

q: Which term matches this definition? “under involuntary control, moves internal organs, cells contain a single nucleus, are spindle-shaped, and do not appear striated; each cell is a fiber”
why: smooth muscle: under involuntary control, moves internal organs, cells contain a single nucleus, are spindle-shaped, and do not appear striated; each cell is a fiber

q: Which term matches this definition? “alignment of parallel actin and myosin filaments which form a banded pattern”
why: striation: alignment of parallel actin and myosin filaments which form a banded pattern

card.q: Watch this video to learn more about muscle tissue. In looking through a microscope how could you distinguish skeletal muscle tissue from smooth muscle?
card.a: Skeletal muscle cells are striated.

card.q: You are watching cells in a dish spontaneously contract. They are all contracting at different rates; some fast, some slow. After a while, several cells link up and they begin contracting in synchrony. Discuss what is going on and what type of cells you are looking at.
card.a: The cells in the dish are cardiomyocytes, cardiac muscle cells. They have an intrinsic ability to contract. When they link up, they form intercalating discs that allow the cells to communicate with each other and begin contracting in synchrony.

card.q: Why does skeletal muscle look striated?
card.a: Under the light microscope, cells appear striated due to the arrangement of the contractile proteins actin and myosin.

q: The cells responsible for the transmission of the nerve impulse are ________.
why: The correct answer is: neurons. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The nerve impulse travels down a(n) ________, away from the cell body.
why: The correct answer is: axon. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following central nervous system cells regulate ions, regulate the uptake and/or breakdown of some neurotransmitters, and contribute to the formation of the blood-brain barrier?
why: The correct answer is: astrocytes. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “star-shaped cell in the central nervous system that regulates ions and uptake and/or breakdown of some neurotransmitters and contributes to the formation of the blood-brain barrier”
why: astrocyte: star-shaped cell in the central nervous system that regulates ions and uptake and/or breakdown of some neurotransmitters and contributes to the formation of the blood-brain barrier

q: Which term matches this definition? “layer of lipid inside some neuroglial cells that wraps around the axons of some neurons”
why: myelin: layer of lipid inside some neuroglial cells that wraps around the axons of some neurons

q: Which term matches this definition? “supportive neural cells”
why: neuroglia: supportive neural cells

q: Which term matches this definition? “excitable neural cell that transfer nerve impulses”

q: Which term matches this definition? “neuroglial cell that produces myelin in the brain”

q: Which term matches this definition? “neuroglial cell that produces myelin in the peripheral nervous system”

card.q: Follow this link to learn more about nervous tissue. What are the main parts of a nerve cell?
card.a: Dendrites, cell body, and the axon.

card.q: Which morphological adaptations of neurons make them suitable for the transmission of nerve impulse?
card.a: Neurons are well suited for the transmission of nerve impulses because short extensions, dendrites, receive impulses from other neurons, while a long tail extension, an axon, carries electrical impulses away from the cell to other neurons.

card.q: What are the functions of astrocytes?
card.a: Astrocytes regulate ions and uptake and/or breakdown of some neurotransmitters and contribute to the formation of the blood-brain-barrier.

q: Which of the following processes is not a cardinal sign of inflammation?
why: The correct answer is: fever. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: When a mast cell reacts to an irritation, which of the following chemicals does it release?
why: The correct answer is: histamine. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Atrophy refers to ________.
why: The correct answer is: loss of mass. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Individuals can slow the rate of aging by modifying all of these lifestyle aspects except for ________.
why: The correct answer is: genetic factors. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which term matches this definition? “programmed cell death”
why: apoptosis: programmed cell death

q: Which term matches this definition? “loss of mass and function”
why: atrophy: loss of mass and function

q: Which term matches this definition? “also called coagulation; complex process by which blood components form a plug to stop bleeding”
why: clotting: also called coagulation; complex process by which blood components form a plug to stop bleeding

q: Which term matches this definition? “chemical compound released by mast cells in response to injury that causes vasodilation and endothelium permeability”
why: histamine: chemical compound released by mast cells in response to injury that causes vasodilation and endothelium permeability

q: Which term matches this definition? “response of tissue to injury”
why: inflammation: response of tissue to injury

q: Which term matches this definition? “accidental death of cells and tissues”

card.q: Watch this video to see the skin healing process. What is the process and how long does it take?
card.a: Approximately one month.

card.q: Watch this video to learn more about tumors. What is a tumor?
card.a: A mass of cancer cells that continue to grow and divide.

card.q: Why is it important to watch for increased redness, swelling and pain after a cut or abrasion has been cleaned and bandaged?
card.a: These symptoms would indicate that infection is present.

card.q: Aspirin is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that inhibits the formation of blood clots and is taken regularly by individuals with a heart condition. Steroids such as cortisol are used to control some autoimmune diseases and severe arthritis by down-regulating the inflammatory response. After reading the role of inflammation in the body’s response to infection, can you predict an undesirable consequence of taking anti-inflammatory drugs on a regular basis?
card.a: Since NSAIDs or other anti-inflammatory drugs inhibit the formation of blood clots, regular and prolonged use of these drugs may promote internal bleeding, such as bleeding in the stomach. Excessive levels of cortisol would suppress inflammation, which could slow the wound healing process.

card.q: As an individual ages, a constellation of symptoms begins the decline to the point where an individual’s functioning is compromised. Identify and discuss two factors that have a role in factors leading to the compromised situation.
card.a: The genetic makeup and the lifestyle of each individual are factors which determine the degree of decline in cells, tissues, and organs as an individual ages.

card.q: Discuss changes that occur in cells as a person ages.
card.a: All cells experience changes with aging. They become larger, and many cannot divide and regenerate. Because of alterations in cell membranes, transport of oxygen and nutrients into the cell and removal of carbon dioxide and waste products are not as efficient in the elderly. Cells lose their ability to function, or they begin to function abnormally, leading to disease and cancer.

q: The papillary layer of the dermis is most closely associated with which layer of the epidermis?
why: The correct answer is: stratum basale. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Langerhans cells are commonly found in the ________.
why: The correct answer is: stratum spinosum. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The papillary and reticular layers of the dermis are composed mainly of ________.
why: The correct answer is: connective tissue. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Collagen lends ________ to the skin.
why: The correct answer is: structure. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Which of the following is not a function of the hypodermis?
options: source of blood vessels in the epidermis
a site to long-term energy storage
why: The correct answer is: source of blood vessels in the epidermis. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

card.q: The skin consists of two layers and a closely associated layer. View this animation to learn more about layers of the skin. What are the basic functions of each of these layers?
card.a: The epidermis provides protection, the dermis provides support and flexibility, and the hypodermis (fat layer) provides insulation and padding.

card.q: If you zoom on the cells at the outermost layer of this section of skin, what do you notice about the cells?
card.a: These cells do not have nuclei, so you can deduce that they are dead. They appear to be sloughing off.

card.q: If you zoom on the cells of the stratum spinosum, what is distinctive about them?
card.a: These cells have desmosomes, which give the cells their spiny appearance.

card.q: This ABC video follows the story of a pair of fraternal African-American twins, one of whom is albino. Watch this video to learn about the challenges these children and their family face. Which ethnicities do you think are exempt from the possibility of albinism?
card.a: There are none.

card.q: What determines the color of skin, and what is the process that darkens skin when it is exposed to UV light?
card.a: The pigment melanin, produced by melanocytes, is primarily responsible for skin color. Melanin comes in different shades of brown and black. Individuals with darker skin have darker, more abundant melanin, whereas fair-skinned individuals have a lighter shade of skin and less melanin. Exposure to UV irradiation stimulates the melanocytes to produce and secrete more melanin.

card.q: Cells of the epidermis derive from stem cells of the stratum basale. Describe how the cells change as they become integrated into the different layers of the epidermis.
card.a: As the cells move into the stratum spinosum, they begin the synthesis of keratin and extend cell processes, desmosomes, which link the cells. As the stratum basale continues to produce new cells, the keratinocytes of the stratum spinosum are pushed into the stratum granulosum. The cells become flatter, their cell membranes thicken, and they generate large amounts of the proteins keratin and keratohyalin. The nuclei and other cell organelles disintegrate as the cells die, leaving behind the keratin, keratohyalin, and cell membranes that form the stratum lucidum and the stratum corneum. The keratinocytes in these layers are mostly dead and flattened. Cells in the stratum corneum are periodically shed.

q: In response to stimuli from the sympathetic nervous system, the arrector pili ________.
options: are glands on the skin surface
why: The correct answer is: are responsible for goose bumps. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: The hair matrix contains ________.
why: The correct answer is: a layer of basal cells. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Eccrine sweat glands ________.
options: are present in the skin throughout the body and produce watery sweat
why: The correct answer is: are present in the skin throughout the body and produce watery sweat. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Sebaceous glands ________.
options: are a type of sweat gland
may function in response to touch
release a watery solution of salt and metabolic waste
why: The correct answer is: are associated with hair follicles. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Similar to the hair, nails grow continuously throughout our lives. Which of the following is furthest from the nail growth center?
why: The correct answer is: hyponychium. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

card.q: Explain the differences between eccrine and apocrine sweat glands.
card.a: Eccrine sweat glands are all over the body, especially the forehead and palms of the hand. They release a watery sweat, mixed with some metabolic waste and antibodies. Apocrine glands are associated with hair follicles. They are larger than eccrine sweat glands and lie deeper in the dermis, sometimes even reaching the hypodermis. They release a thicker sweat that is often decomposed by bacteria on the skin, resulting in an unpleasant odor.

card.q: Describe the structure and composition of nails.
card.a: Nails are composed of densely packed dead keratinocytes. They protect the fingers and toes from mechanical stress. The nail body is formed on the nail bed, which is at the nail root. Nail folds, folds of skin that overlap the nail on its side, secure the nail to the body. The crescent-shaped region at the base of the nail is the lunula.

q: In humans, exposure of the skin to sunlight is required for ________.
why: The correct answer is: vitamin D synthesis. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: One of the functions of the integumentary system is protection. Which of the following does not directly contribute to that function?
why: The correct answer is: folic acid synthesis. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: An individual using a sharp knife notices a small amount of blood where he just cut himself. Which of the following layers of skin did he have to cut into in order to bleed?
why: The correct answer is: papillary dermis. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: As you are walking down the beach, you see a dead, dry, shriveled-up fish. Which layer of your epidermis keeps you from drying out?
why: The correct answer is: stratum corneum. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: If you cut yourself and bacteria enter the wound, which of the following cells would help get rid of the bacteria?
why: The correct answer is: Langerhans cells. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

card.q: Why do people sweat excessively when exercising outside on a hot day?
card.a: Sweating cools the body when it becomes warm. When the body temperature rises, such as when exercising on a hot day, the dermal blood vessels dilate, and the sweat glands begin to secrete more sweat. The evaporation of the sweat from the surface of the skin cools the body by dissipating heat.

card.q: Explain your skin’s response to a drop in body core temperature.
card.a: When the core body temperature drops, the body switches to heat-conservation mode. This can include an inhibition to excessive sweating and a decrease of blood flow to the papillary layers of the skin. This reduction of blood flow helps conserve body heat.

q: In general, skin cancers ________.
options: are easily treatable and not a major health concern
can be reduced by limiting exposure to the sun
why: The correct answer is: can be reduced by limiting exposure to the sun. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: Bedsores ________.
options: can be treated with topical moisturizers
are preventable by eliminating pressure points
why: The correct answer is: are preventable by eliminating pressure points. Re-read the lesson above to see why.

q: An individual has spent too much time sun bathing. Not only is their skin painful to touch, but small blisters have appeared in the affected area. This indicates that they have damaged which layers of skin?
why: The correct answer is: epidermis and dermis. Re-read the lesson above to see why.
